page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration belonging to the AMD EPYC-based N2D instance family. It provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using multithreading, alongside 32 GB of system memory. This establishes a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an x86_64 architecture with 32 KB L1 data cache, 512 KB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with support for cryptographic instruction sets such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as AVX, BMI2, and FMA vector extensions. The instance carries no local storage volumes and includes no hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-thread performance alongside limited parallel throughput due to the small 4-vCPU count. The instance achieves a strong stress-ng single-core score of 2,681.08, ranking in the top 25%, while its multi-core stress-ng result of 5,386.56 falls into the lower 25%. Similarly, Geekbench scores show mid-tier single-core execution at 1,426.0 and a multi-core score of 3,257.0. Memory throughput reaches 28.03 GB/s for large-block writes and 38.56 GB/s for uncached reads, delivering consistent middle-tier behavior across memory-dependent benchmarks and single-threaded data compression routines.

From an efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-4 provides an economical option for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand massive parallel compute capacity. Because core count is constrained to 4 vCPUs, operations with high thread concurrency—such as intensive multi-threaded decompression, large-scale software builds, and heavy database query concurrency—exhibit lower throughput relative to wider compute profiles. However, applications requiring dedicated physical cores and generous memory capacity per thread benefit from its hardware distribution.

Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is best suited for small-to-medium in-memory caches, light database instances, memory-heavy microservices, background job workers, and memory-constrained ETL tasks requiring stable single-core frequency and elevated RAM allocations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 32 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes local disk storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded compute capacity, reflected by an upper-quartile stress-ng single-core result of 2,681.08, balanced against modest multi-threaded throughput across multi-core tests and database operations. Memory performance remains stable with a 2,030.58 PassMark memory index and 28.03 GB/s large-block write speeds. This profile provides a balanced, cost-effective infrastructure layer tailored for memory-bound tasks requiring moderate processing overhead, including in-memory caches, light database management systems, and memory-intensive data ingestion workers.
